highlights.title: KP promises to challenge McCullum as England push to be 'world's best'
highlights.summary: Kevin Pietersen has promised to challenge England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum in his new role as a specialist mentor to the team, saying it's precisely why he was brought in.
body: Since retiring as a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after McCullum had just taken over.

Pietersen's work with England began with a 3-0 T20 series whitewash of Sri Lanka, before the hosts then also clinched a 2-1 ODI series success over the same side on Sunday. His role with the team will continue through to the 2027 50-over World Cup in just over a year's time.

"Brendon, when he first called me, I thought I was in trouble because I'd said something, but he said this exact point: 'I'd like you to come in and challenge me,'" Pietersen told Sky Sports Cricket ahead of England's series-clinching 223-run win over Sri Lanka at The Oval.
"He's since said to me: 'I absolutely love the fact that you are inside the rooms and you are picking on things that can make the players better.'

highlights.title: Coke Plus is the fibermaxxing soda that Americans haven’t caught on to yet
highlights.summary: On a recent trip to Japan, I found a fiber-forward soda that tastes like Diet Coke and keeps things moving. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: On my recent vacation to Japan, I learned they are light-years ahead of the US in many ways – from their high-tech toilets and efficient bullet trains to … diet sodas.

Amidst the chilled bottles of Coke Zero and Sugar-Free Pepsi stocked in the fridge of practically every 7-Eleven was another mysterious beverage in a bright white can – Coke Plus, which my friend heard about from the internet’s goldmine of travel videos.

Unlike Coca-Cola’s other diet sodas, Coke Plus has 5g of indigestible dextrin fiber, which it says can “suppress the absorption of fat from food and moderate neutral fat level spikes in the blood after eating”. Its target market? Adults 40 and up.

Coke Plus was ahead of its time. It debuted in Japan in 2017, before the fibermaxxing craze came to the US. Its launch attracted national attention, earning coverage in outlets such as New York Magazine and Business Insider. Despite the buzz, it never enjoyed a wide US release. Japan’s demographic skews older – over a quarter of its residents are at least 65 years old – which may, in part, explain its popularity.

highlights.title: Kohli passes 15,000 ODI runs as hundred helps India beat West Indies
highlights.summary: Virat Kohli celebrated his return to the international arena by hitting his 55th ODI hundred as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the series opener on Sunday.
body: India's star batter - who now only plays this format in international cricket - smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, including 10 fours and nine sixes, as India successfully chased down 296 in just 41.4 overs.
In doing so, the 37-year-old also became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar (18,426) to pass 15,000 runs in ODIs.

"My focus has never been on milestones. Just looking back at the start of my journey, it makes me feel very grateful," Kohli said. "I enjoy each and every minute that I am out there playing for India, and I am able to do the job for my team. As a cricketer, this is all I could dream of."
Skipper Shubman Gill also notched a century, scoring 110 off 108 deliveries as India registered an easy win - clinched with a Kohli six - to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

highlights.title: 13 Years Ago, One Dark JRPG Proved Atlus Could Still Be Hardcore
highlights.summary: Today, we recognize Atlus for the Persona, Etrian Odyssey, and Trauma Center franchises, as well as for the years it spent publishing interesting RPGs from smaller Japanese developers that otherwise might never have made it to North America. That history is worthwhile.
body: Released on May 23, 2013, in Japan and brought west two months later, Shin Megami Tensei 4 was the follow-up fans had been craving for the better part of a decade. Instead of visits to hot springs and the beach, players navigated the hellscape that once had been Tokyo. They roamed foreboding corridors populated by demons out for blood, recruiting some of them while facing the possible extinction of humanity itself.

As later proved by 2021’s Shin Megami Tensei 5, Atlus has managed to keep both the Shin Megami Tensei and Persona franchises going strong. But Shin Megami Tensei 4 launched when that future was in doubt, and it did so on the last piece of hardware you might expect: the Nintendo 3DS. The game was dark and brutal, just like Nocturne. It launched with a CD full of eerie musical selections, as well as a 176-page “Strategy & Design Book” produced with strategy publisher Prima Games.

highlights.title: Out of the Park Baseball lets me enjoy baseball even when the Mets suck
highlights.summary: If you were to ask me what game or game series I've sunk the most time into, the answer would be easy: Out of the Park Baseball ( OOTP ). I have spent roughly 2,300 hours, according to Steam, playing various editions of the game. OOTP isn't like MLB The Show or Super Mega Baseball.
body: OOTP Baseball is a nitty gritty hyper-realistic baseball sim that puts you in the GMs office.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

You can play individual games and dig into play-by-play managing in OOTP if you want. But that becomes tedious. And frankly, it’s not where the game is the most fun. Instead, I think the game is at its best when you sit in the GM’s chair and maybe make some helpful “suggestions” about how to structure the lineup or bullpen.

The UI is complicated and dense. 90 percent of the time, you’re just looking at rows of stats and scouting reports. And the level of detail is deep. OOTP includes not just current MLB players, but historical MLB players, all minor league teams, Korea’s KBO League, and even the entire World Baseball Classic.

highlights.title: Australia suffer ODI series defeat to South Africa
highlights.summary: Australia fell to an ODI series defeat to South Africa with a game to spare as they were beaten by 32 runs in the second ODI match of three in Johannesburg on Sunday.
body: David Miller (142 off 93 balls) and Temba Bavuma (103 off 116) each smashed centuries for South Africa as they set the visitors a massive 366-run target after being inserted at the toss.
Australia looked well placed early on in their reply, with openers Mitch Marsh (84 off 53) and ​Travis Head (85 off 76) setting the tone by blazing the bowling to all parts.

But ultimately the tourists' middle-order batting issues and struggles against spin were again laid bare. From 191-2 in the 25th over, they added only 62 for the loss of four wickets in the next 15 and a bit overs to stumble to 253-6.

That left Australia needing another 113 runs to win from the final 10 overs and, despite a late counter-punch from Xavier Bartlett (50 off 28), they'd eventually be bowled out for 333 in the final over.

highlights.title: The pain of letting go of a loved one’s belongings | Letters
highlights.summary: Readers respond to Polly Hudson’s article about disposing of her late mother’s possessions. Reading Polly Hudson’s account of clearing her mother’s house ( My mum has died – and every decision I make about her belongings feels wrong, 20 September ) made me think about my experience of doing the…
body: I was determined to recycle as much as possible, feeding the good things through to charity shops and going back later to see what had and hadn’t sold. When one charity shop in the Welsh border town where my mother lived didn’t want her manual typewriter, on the grounds that nobody would have use for it, I took it to a charity shop in London, which snapped it up and put it in the window.

Polly Hudson’s final paragraph is spot-on. So long as you have the physical space, it’s not a “now or never” thing. I went through my mother’s things in waves. Many items that were impossible to throw out the first time around had became less so when I revisited them a few months or a year later. It was a gradual process that felt reliable.

My sister and I evolved the concept of the “family archive”. So much that we as children were familiar with – such as what our parents looked like on holiday in their 40s – is fascinating to grandchildren who have only known them in old age, and the next generation will perhaps never have seen them at all.

highlights.summary: Amazon UK is already dropping the price on a few grooming essentials ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, and this Philips Multigroom 7000 Series is currently £51.99, down from £94.99.
body: That's a pretty substantial £43 saving on an all-in-one trimmer designed to cover pretty much everything, from your beard and hair to your nose, ears and body. It comes with 17 attachments and 26 length settings ranging from 0.5mm to 20mm, so there's plenty of room to get the exact trim you're after without needing a drawer full of different gadgets.

The Multigroom 7000 uses self-sharpening full-metal steel blades, which Philips says stay as sharp as they were on day one without needing blade oil. There's also BeardSense technology, which scans beard density 125 times per second and automatically increases power when it detects thicker or longer hair.

For more precise work, the included precision comb offers 11 length settings between 1mm and 3mm in 0.2mm increments. There's also a narrow detail trimmer for sharper lines and finer work, alongside a metal trimmer for tidying up your cheeks, chin and neck.

At £51.99, it's a decent chunk below its usual £94.99 price, although it's worth remembering that Prime Big Deal Days itself doesn't officially start until October 6. Whether this particular deal sticks around until then, or gets replaced by an even lower price, remains to be seen.

highlights.title: Engram is a sampler that turns broken AI hallucinations into music
highlights.summary: Music startup Thoughtful Things has just launched the Kickstarter campaign for its first instrument, Engram. It's a sampler and groovebox that uses AI to mangle incoming audio and even hallucinate completely new sounds. This isn't Suno in a box, though.
body: Thoughtful Things says Engram is a ‘field recorder for latent space’ and circuit-bending tiny AI models.

“We’ve trained our audio models on open datasets that only contain audio licensed for commercial use (CC-BY or similar). We have not trained and will never train our models on non-commercial, pirated, or otherwise stolen data.”

The company also plans to open up Engram’s firmware so that others can tweak it or load their own custom models. In the campaign video, founder Evan King uses his voice to ask for “piano,” and Engram spits out something glitchy and vaguely piano-like. He says to think of Engram as a “field recorder for latent space.” It’s about exploring the world of AI hallucinations and experimental sound design. It even draws inspiration from circuit bending, allowing you to tweak and even break its tiny AI models.

Thoughtful Things is launching with a limited run of Engrams for the Kickstarter campaign, starting at $675. The company hasn’t said what the retail price will be, though it’s likely to be between $850 and $900, as the $675 pledge is listed as a 30 percent discount.

body: Dimitris Kourbelis scored the only goal in the 74th minute, earning Greece their first-ever victory in 11 matches against Germany. Ivan Jovanovic’s side now lead ⁠Group A2 with six points ⁠from two matches; Klopp’s side are third with one point from two games after a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands on Thursday.

The hosts were in control for most of the game and had close to 80% possession in the first half alone. Germany were ultimately punished ⁠for sloppy defending, especially in the second half, which gave the visitors space to attack.

Felix Nmecha fired wide in the 54th minute, moments after the Greece keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis ‌had palmed a Joshua Kimmich free kick over the bar. The Greeks then almost scored in the 66th after Kimmich lost possession in his own half, but substitute Fotis Ioannidis fired just wide of the post.

They did better eight minutes later, with Kourbelis’ deflected low drive earning their second victory in a row after their last-gasp 2-1 win over Serbia on Thursday. Greece will now host the Dutch on Thursday, while Germany host Serbia.

highlights.title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
highlights.summary: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment, hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models.
body: OpenAI keeps uncovering incidents of its models behaving in ‘unexpected or concerning’ ways.

In addition, OpenAI revealed on Friday that its agents had inappropriately uploaded 53nimages from ChatGPT users to image-hosting sites. The company has not stated if the images were AI-generated, photos, or contained identifiable people. The company also revealed Friday that its models had attempted to hack the Department of Education’s website, and pulled data from the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The revelations are part of an ongoing review by OpenAI into the behavior of its models. As it dug into its records, following the Hugging Face hack, it’s uncovered more and more instances of “unexpected or concerning behavior.” It’s evidence not just of how difficult AI agents are becoming to control as they grow more advanced, but also of the challenge of tracking their actions. Their behavior can be unpredictable, and they’re smart enough to try and cover their tracks. This has led to growing calls from researchers, those within the industry, and even some CEOs to call for slowing the pace of AI advancement.

highlights.summary: In the new DreamWorks animated movie Forgotten Island, the two teenage leads, Jo and Raissa, say the same phrase to each other over and over: “Tayo na!” As with a lot of the other Filipino cultural elements in the movie, writer-directors Joel Crawford and Januel P.
body: But that can be a little difficult when the context changes from scene to scene — and when the phrase itself has a variety of meanings. As Filipinos and Tagalog speakers have been explaining online, “Tayo na!” can colloquially mean “Let’s go!” or “You and me!” or “Get up!” depending on pronunciation, who’s speaking, and whether there’s a romantic, parental, or other context.

Forgotten Island uses the phrase in a lot of different ways as Jo and Raissa, two childhood friends confronting hidden tensions and big changes in their relationship, either urge each other into adventure or rev each other up in the face of danger. The first time Jo says it, when she first meets Raissa, she actually says, "Let's go! Tayo na!" It seems very casual at first, but throughout the movie, it takes on new weight and bigger meanings.
The characters’ voice actors, Liza Soberano (Raissa) and singer-songwriter H.E.R. (Jo), tell Polygon that their own Filipino roots played into how they interpreted the phrase from scene to scene.

highlights.title: Can Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince save the web from AI?
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with Matthew Prince, who is CEO of Cloudflare. This episode is part of a two-part series on the future of business. Matthew last joined us on the show about two and a half years ago, at what we thought then was a wild pivot point for the internet — and now it
body: Cloudflare found in June that bots made up more than half of internet traffic. That number just keeps going up as more and more AI companies scrape more and more of the web, and now as more and more AI agents try and do things for people on the web. Cloudflare sits between websites and all those agents, and allows website owners some level of control: Owners can block all those AI tools, allow them, or, as you’ll hear, only allow those that might pay money for access.

So Matthew and I talked about how to control all these bots, what kind of mess they’re making of the web, and what kinds of information might be valuable in the future as some of the payment schemes come into focus. You’ll hear me ask pretty directly if some of the outcomes he’s describing are actually good — Matthew is a thoughtful guy, and his answer is something I’m still thinking about well after we had this conversation.

highlights.title: McTominay’s role a poser for Pocognoli as Scotland offer positives in Slovenia
highlights.summary: New coach still learning about his squad as they prepare to face Switzerland with the Napoli midfielder expected to return in November. An elongated international window does not prevent Sébastien Pocognoli from glancing towards the next one.
body: The scoreless draw in Slovenia on Saturday raised the question of where McTominay will fit in when he returns. “He can play in many positions,” Pocognoli said. “He is a top player so he can read the game. We will see.”

Indeed we will. The answer is not immediately obvious. Pocognoli deployed Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson as central midfielders in Ljubljana with John McGinn placed ahead of them to support a two-man strike force. Gilmour was heavily influential during Scotland’s impressive second half. Ferguson’s combative and defensive skills are valuable. McGinn, like McTominay, is a mainstay of the team. It is therefore legitimate to ask how Pocognoli handles McTominay, who is expected to return to the Scotland scene in November.

“For now we just need to put the structure in place,” Pocognoli said. “I hope Scott watched the game and thought ‘OK, I see myself in that shape in the second half’, and that with good discipline he can enjoy it. I hope he can look and think: ‘Yeah, I want to play.’
“Andy Robertson was really positive after the game and said that he really enjoyed it. It is really good to hear that from top players.”

highlights.title: Does GLP-1 use result in significant hair loss?

About 20 million people across the US, UK, and EU are taking GLP-1 receptor agonists like tirzepatide and semaglutide (Ozempic or Mounjaro are common brands) for weight loss…
body: In one survey of people who take these medications, 20% of respondents experienced hair shedding, although the lack of high-quality data from a randomized, controlled trial to assess this side-effect makes it difficult to know exactly how common it is.

While GLP-1-related hair loss is often temporary and reversible, it’s significant enough that some patients hesitate to take drugs they would otherwise benefit from using. Here’s what you need to know.
Most people who take GLP-1 drugs don’t have hair loss. However, those who do often notice it within the first year, usually peaking a little before the 12th month.
